instruction: Access the Slide Master through View > Master > Slide Master, then modify the slide number to have red font color

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Another paraphrase of original task - 'modify' instead of 'change'. The evaluator uses the existing check_page_number_colors function to verify red color in slide master.
metadata.verification: The check_page_number_colors function from slides.py (lines 876-920) parses the slide master XML to find the color of the page number placeholder. It checks the second-to-last solidFill/srgbClr element in the slide master and verifies it matches the expected color using threshold-based RGB comparison (red: R > G+50 and R > B+50, blue: B > G+50 and B > R+50, green: G > R+50 and G > B+50, black: R < 50 and G < 50 and B < 50).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the slide master page number color modification
Getter (get_vm_file) appropriately retrieves the PPTX file after saving via postconfig
Metric (check_page_number_colors) parses slide master XML and checks color using threshold-based RGB comparison
Expected value {'color': 'red'} correctly specifies the required color
Postconfig includes file save (Ctrl+S) which is necessary for XML changes to persist
Coverage is complete: checks slide master modification and red color requirement
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The metric function uses hardcoded index [-2] to access the second-to-last color element in slide master XML. This is fragile and assumes a specific XML structure. Consider adding validation to check that color_elems has at least 2 elements before accessing [-2], or make the element selection more robust by searching for the page number placeholder specifically rather than relying on positional indexing.

The hardcoded index approach may fail if different PPTX templates have different numbers of color elements in the slide master. A more robust approach would be to search for the page number shape by name or type, then extract its color.
